resources.string: Done
After a rehearsal
1. Let WakeNudge come back to the front
Allow \"Display over other apps\" for WakeNudge. Then, if you leave an alarm while it rings, its screen comes back. Nothing is drawn over other apps.
Open the setting
If the switch was greyed out or a message said it is restricted: Android blocks this for apps not from a store. Tap OK on that message, then press Next.
Next
In App info, tap the three dots, top right, then Allow restricted settings, then confirm with your fingerprint or PIN. Then come back here.
Back to the setting
Now switch on \"Display over other apps\" again. It should work this time.
2. Battery: unrestricted
So Android does not hold WakeNudge back overnight.
3. Notifications on
The ring notification is what wakes the screen when the phone is locked.
4. Full-screen alarm
Lets the alarm screen open over the lock screen.
Fix
5. Try it now

A real ring of the alarm in 5 seconds, with its missions, so you know you can finish it before anything hard to undo. It has no snooze and gives up after 10 minutes. Emergency and the way out work as on a real morning.
Set an alarm with a mission first.
Try it now
Rehearsed
Rings in a few seconds. Lock the phone if you like.
Android refused to set the rehearsal. Check Alarm Health.
6. Block force stop and uninstall

Turns on device admin for WakeNudge. While it is on, Android won\'t let you force-stop or uninstall WakeNudge. It doesn\'t stop the phone being switched off. Turn it off here any time an alarm isn\'t ringing or snoozed, or in Settings, Security, Device admin apps at any time.
Finish one rehearsal first (step 5), so you know you can end the alarm before you make it harder to remove.
If Android says this is restricted, use \"Allow restricted settings\" in App info as in step 1, then try again.
Turn on
Turn off
On: Force stop and uninstall are blocked. The Force stop button may still look available, but it does nothing.
Off
An alarm is ringing or snoozed. Finish it first, then turn this off here. You can also turn it off now in Settings, Security, Device admin apps.
You can always turn it off in Settings, Security, Device admin apps (on some phones: Security and privacy, More security settings, Device admin apps).
Device admin is off. Force stop and uninstall work again.
Android didn\'t turn it off. Use Settings, Security, Device admin apps.

WakeNudge asks for no device admin powers at all: it can\'t wipe, lock or watch your phone. Being active only means Android won\'t let you force-stop or uninstall it. Turn it off here at any time, or in WakeNudge\'s Protection screen when no alarm is ringing or snoozed.
Stops a half-asleep force stop or uninstall of your alarm. No device powers are used.
Your alarms can then be force-stopped or uninstalled again.
What this doesn\'t stop

Power off isn\'t blocked. Holding the power button, the power menu or a voice assistant can switch the phone off or restart it. When the phone starts again, the alarm rings again at full volume with no snooze, as many times as the alarm allows.

A phone that stays off can\'t ring. Safe mode, a factory reset, a computer with USB debugging and a flat battery also beat it. Do Not Disturb set to Total Silence can silence alarms. Extreme Battery Saver pauses apps you haven\'t chosen as essential, so add WakeNudge to that list. Emergency calls always work.

If I get stuck it\'s on me. Emergency and the backup mission stay.
